title: EOIP Common Definitions
description: Reusable type definitions shared across all EOIP data contracts. Import via $ref to enforce consistent patterns for identifiers, timestamps, confidence scores, URNs, and provenance references.

canonical_id.description: Platform-wide unique identifier. Preferred format is URN (urn:eoip:{domain}:{type}:{local-id}); legacy short-form IDs are also accepted.

entity_type.description: PascalCase vertex label from the enterprise ontology (e.g. CodeFile, JiraIssue, Person).

relationship_type.description: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE edge label from the enterprise ontology (e.g. DEPENDS_ON, AUTHORED_BY).

graph_domain.description: Logical partition of the enterprise graph. Each domain groups related entity/relationship types.

confidence.description: Calibrated probability score. 0.0 = no evidence, 1.0 = deterministic/human-confirmed.

confidence_nullable.description: Optional confidence score; null when confidence is not applicable or not yet computed.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of the data contract (major.minor).

tenant_id.description: Namespace-level tenant identifier for multi-tenant isolation.

provenance_ref.description: URI or path pointing to the original source of a fact (e.g. git commit SHA, Jira issue URL, document path).

provenance_refs.description: Ordered list of provenance references establishing the evidence chain.

hash_hex.description: SHA-256 hex digest used for content addressing and integrity verification.

risk_level.description: Qualitative risk classification per NIST SP 800-30 / ISO 31000.

creation_status.description: How this record was created: deterministic extraction, ML/heuristic inference, or human review.

deletion_policy.description: Governs when this record may be garbage-collected.

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the result set.

pagination.description: Standard pagination envelope for list/search responses.

field.description: JSON Pointer to the offending field, if applicable.

error_detail.description: Structured error following RFC 7807 / EOIP error contract.
